subject: Problem with using pbdNCDF4::nc_create_par or pbdNCDF4::ncvar_put

messages.author: d397e97f838d60b9
messages.subject: Problem with using pbdNCDF4::nc_create_par or pbdNCDF4::ncvar_put
parts:
Hi all - 

I am facing an issue while using my freshly compiled version of pbdNCDF4. I dont really know if the issue is technical (depends of the compilation) or rather on the scheme of my algorithm.
The following is what I try to do, mixing both Rmpi and pbdNCDF4.

I got a ncfile(A) with 3938(N) x 455884(T) records. 
I must create (B) from (A), by applying a marginal transformation for each n in (N).

To do so, I am using Rmpi and assign the transformation f(n) for each task n to a pool of worker.  n >> nbworkers.
Once f(n) is computed by a worker, it sends the result back to the master process which save the result into a netcdf-file (B). This code is already working but is very slow. To avoid concurrency the master open the file, write the vector and close the file for each received result.

Since the writing of each column  (i.e. the result of f(n) composed of 455884 elements, for each n in N) is the bottleneck of my code, I would like to use pbdNCDF4 to write them no more from the master process but from each worker, independently.

Hence the code is (summed up) as follow :
Master
[...]
dimNode <- ncdim_def("node", "count", node, create_dimvar = TRUE) ##### 1 #####
dimTime <- ncdim_def("time", units.time, time, create_dimvar = TRUE)
varStandardScale <- ncvar_def(var, "", list(dimNode,dimTime), missval=missval, prec="float", compression = 9)
out.nc <- pbdNCDF4::nc_create_par(file.out, list(varStandardScale), verbose= TRUE)
out.nc <- nc_create(standardizedfile,list(varStandardScaleX))
nc_close(out.nc)
[...] master sends tasks to worker [...]
Once all tasks are performed it gets the hand back.
[...]
Worker(s)
[...] get a task n to process, and compute x.standard for this margin
out.nc <- pbdNCDF4::nc_open_par(filename = file.out, write = TRUE, readunlim = FALSE, verbose= TRUE)
pbdNCDF4::nc_var_par_access(var, collective=FALSE) # make the process independent. Correct ?
pbdNCDF4::ncvar_put(out.nc, var, x.standard, start=c(n,1), count=c(1,-1)) ##### 2 #####
nc_close(out.nc)
[...] loop to process a new task if exist, otherwise shutdown the worker.


Errors that I get are 
[...]
Error in R_nc4_enddef: NetCDF: HDF error
Error in R_nc4_sync: NetCDF: HDF error
Error in paste("file", filename, "is format", nc$format) :  
  object 'filename' not found

for ##### 1 ##### ,


and

[...]
Error in R_nc4_put_vara_double: NetCDF: HDF error
Error in pbdNCDF4::ncvar_put(out.nc, paste0(var, "_standard"), rep(1,  :  
  C function R_nc4_put_var_double returned error

for  ##### 2 #####.

This is clearly a HDF5 error, but beyond that I cannot say anything...


To check the installation, I performed the tests from the manual

> mpiexec -np 2 Rscript -e "demo(ncwrite_par,'pbdNCDF4',ask=F,echo=F)"
> mpiexec -np 2 Rscript -e "demo(ncread_par,'pbdNCDF4',ask=F,echo=F)"

 to test the parallel functions, and they are working perfectly. 


Any advice would be very appreciate ! 
Thanks !
R.

messages.author: b3fada61390d545a
messages.subject: Re: [RBigData] Problem with using pbdNCDF4::nc_create_par or pbdNCDF4::ncvar_put
parts:
Hi Romain,

Instead of using a master-workers approach with Rmpi, I would suggest an SPMD approach with pbdMPI. There is no need for a master and you only need SPMD workers. You only write one code and run it in batch. Use the pbdMPI function get.jid() to split the N work between the SPMD workers. Check the demo directory in the pbdNCDF4 package and pbdMPI examples in the pbdDEMO vignette.

The reason for HDF5 failing is that your master runs ncdim_def, ncvar_def, etc. but these are not known to the workers when you do ncvar_put. When you write one code to run SPMD, everyone will run these and everyone will know these.

George

require(pbdMPI, quietly = TRUE)
require(pbdNCDF4, quietly = TRUE)
init()

prec <- "single"
missval <- 1.e30
A <- "A.nc"
B <- "B.nc"

# READ DIMs FROM A
in.nc <- nc_open_par(filename = A, readunlim = FALSE)
node <- ncvar_get(in.nc,"node")
time <- ncvar_get(in.nc,"time")
for (i in 1:in.nc$ndim) {
  d <- in.nc$dim[[i]]
  if (d$name %in% "time") {units.time <- d$units ;break}
}
nc_close(in.nc)

# CREATE NEW FILE B
dimNode <- ncdim_def("node", "count", node, create_dimvar = TRUE)
dimTime <- ncdim_def("time", units.time, time, create_dimvar = TRUE)

transformed.var <- ncvar_def("var_standard", "", list(dimNode,dimTime), missval=missval, prec="float", compression = 9)
out.nc <- pbdNCDF4::nc_create_par(B, list(transformed.var), verbose= TRUE)
nc_close(out.nc)

finalize()

parts:
If you don't have parallel file system with multiple reader/writer, then pbdNCDF4 will not save too much time for you.
If you have, then drop Rmpi. Master has at least 2 comm running, but not workers. It is not wise to choose that way to write in parallel.
